name: Assam Monsoon Flooding and Guwahati Landslide Zone
description: Assam is currently experiencing a fresh spell of monsoon flooding, affecting over 25,000 people across seven districts with the Dhansiri and Katakhal rivers flowing above danger levels. Recent heavy rainfall also triggered deadly landslides in Guwahati. The region faces persistent risks from annual floods, and is situated in Seismic Zone V, making it highly vulnerable to major earthquakes and associated hazards like liquefaction and landslides.

name: Luni River Basin Anomalous Monsoon Flash Flood Zone
description: Barmer faces sudden desert flash flooding and river overflows along the ephemeral Luni River basin due to intense anomalous monsoon rain spells. Normally arid sandy terrain suffers rapid surface run-off and inundation in low-lying salt flats (Rann areas), stranding agricultural settlements and rural transport networks.

name: Ganga-Kosi-Gandak River Basins Active Flood Zone
description: Bihar is currently experiencing critical flood conditions with the Ganga, Kosi, Gandak, and other major rivers flowing significantly above danger marks, impacting at least 13 districts including Patna, Bhagalpur, and Muzaffarpur. This is exacerbated by heavy monsoon rainfall and recent flash floods originating from Nepal. The region also faces a high baseline risk from earthquakes, with most areas falling into seismic zones IV and V, and localized landslide susceptibility.

name: Barak River Valley Active Monsoon Flood and Inundation Zone
description: Cachar is suffering widespread monsoon inundation from the swollen Barak River and its tributaries, submerging agricultural tracts and residential wards across Silchar sub-division. Continuous rain in headwater catchment areas has breached local embankments, raising flash flood risks and waterlogging in low-lying rural blocks.

name: Rishi Ganga Basin Glacial Outburst and Flash Flood Zone
description: Chamoli is under heightened alert for Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and rapid flash flooding in the Rishi Ganga and Dhauli Ganga river basins following active glacial lake expansion in the Nanda Devi sanctuary region. Ongoing monsoon downpours have triggered localized rock-ice avalanches and secondary slope failures threatening downstream hydro projects.

name: Trishuli-Narayani River Basin Active Flood Zone, Chitwan
description: Chitwan district is currently experiencing the aftermath of a major flash flood event from August 26, 2026, originating from a glacial collapse upstream in the Bhotekoshi/Trishuli river system, which flows into the Narayani River. This event caused significant casualties and widespread disruption, including blocked road access due to landslides and erosion. The region is also under ongoing monsoon conditions, increasing the risk of further localized flooding and landslides, alongside a baseline medium seismic hazard.

name: Teesta River Basin Landslide and Highway Inundation Zone

The turbulent Teesta River basin is flowing near warning levels, causing bank erosion and threatening major transportation links connecting Kalimpong and Sikkim.

name: South Gujarat Monsoon Flood & Cyclone Risk Zone
description: This zone in South Gujarat, encompassing areas around Surat, Navsari, and Valsad, experienced severe monsoon flooding in late July and early August 2026, leading to urban waterlogging, infrastructure damage, and mass evacuations. The region remains susceptible to floods and flash floods during the ongoing monsoon season, with post-flood health concerns in affected areas like Bharuch. Additionally, it faces a high baseline risk from cyclones originating in the Arabian Sea, which have shown increased frequency and intensity.

name: Himachal Pradesh Active Monsoon Flood & Landslide Zone
description: Himachal Pradesh is currently experiencing widespread flash floods and landslides triggered by persistent heavy monsoon rainfall, leading to significant road closures, infrastructure damage, and casualties across districts like Mandi, Shimla, Kullu, and Solan. The region also faces inherent high seismic risk and increasing threats from glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs).

description: Joshimath faces severe active land subsidence and structural cracking across municipal wards caused by subterranean water seepage, slope destabilization, and heavy monsoon run-off above the Alaknanda riverbed. The town sits on ancient landslide debris in a highly active seismic zone, accelerating building distress and emergency evacuation alerts.

name: Kathmandu Valley Monsoon Flood and Landslide Risk Zone
description: The Kathmandu Valley is currently experiencing heightened risks from monsoon-induced floods and landslides, with recent heavy rainfall causing road blockages on major highways connecting to the capital and localized disruptions within the valley. This region also faces a critical long-term threat from seismic activity, including potential for soil liquefaction, due to its location in a highly active Himalayan belt and dense, vulnerable urban development.

name: Bhuj Fault Seismic Zone and Arabian Sea Cyclonic Inundation Risk
description: Kutch is situated in a highly active intraplate tectonic setting (Seismic Zone V) along the Kutch Mainland Fault and Katrol Hill Fault systems, with ongoing micro-seismicity and severe historic earthquake vulnerability. The district also faces compound coastal cyclone threats from the Arabian Sea, driving storm surges across the Great Rann mudflats.

name: Indus River Tributary Cloudburst and Glacial Outburst Zone
description: Leh is highly susceptible to sudden high-altitude cloudbursts and violent debris flows along Indus River mountain streams, causing rapid mudslide inundation in urban valley floors. Rapid warming and glacial retreat across the Karakoram-Himalayan range also trigger GLOF alerts and permafrost slope destabilization.

description: Pokhara is currently experiencing heightened landslide activity, with a fatal incident reported today, September 4, 2026, near the city, and a recent partial blockage of the Seti River due to a landslide on July 19, 2026. The region is also under continuous threat from monsoon-induced heavy rainfall, increasing the risk of localized flash floods and debris flows. Underlying these immediate concerns is a very high seismic risk due to its location on a major fault line.

Steep Himalayan topography and rapid melt exacerbate secondary risks of destructive landslides and debris flows, alongside high baseline seismic risk.

name: Alaknanda-Bhagirathi River Basins Multi-Hazard Zone
description: Uttarakhand is currently experiencing widespread heavy rainfall, leading to flash floods, active landslides, and swollen rivers, with the Alaknanda, Mandakini, and Bhagirathi rivers reported to be flowing at or above danger levels. Recent incidents include a massive landslide in Uttarkashi damaging homes and multiple fatalities from rain-related events across the state. The region also faces a critical long-term risk from seismic activity, with the entire state now classified in Seismic Zone V, and an accelerating threat of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) due to rapid glacier melt in areas like the Bhilangana Valley.

name: Chooralmala-Meppadi Active Landslide and Iruvaipuzha Flood Zone
description: Wayanad is currently experiencing catastrophic monsoon landslides and massive debris flows along the Chooralmala, Mundakkai, and Meppadi hillsides, triggered by extreme 24-hour rainfall. The overflowing Iruvaipuzha River has severely inundated low-lying settlements, destroying critical bridge infrastructure and leaving vulnerable hill communities isolated.
